terms.gloss: the features of the face; the lines of a face or a body
terms.comment: Of the face, ōris līneāmenta; of the whole body, corporis (Liv. 26.41, Lewis & Short). The singular līneāmentum is a drawn line.

terms.gloss: the face, the features; also the mouth
terms.comment: With vultus, the expression (see face), it gives a person’s looks: ōs vultumque referre, to have someone’s face and features.

phrases.latin: Hamilcarem juvenem redditum sibi veterēs mīlitēs crēdere, eundem vigōrem in vultū vimque in oculīs, habitum ōris līneāmentaque intuērī
phrases.english: the old soldiers thought Hamilcar had been given back to them young: they saw the same vigour in his face, the same force in his eyes, the same expression and features

phrases.latin: quae nōn minus mōrēs ejus quam ōs vultumque referēbat, tōtumque patrem mīrā similitūdine exscrīpserat
phrases.english: she had his character no less than his face and features, and was the very copy of her father
